proof_attempt_summary: The exact frozen SoftBart posterior was analyzed through full scale integration, rank-grid approximation, weighted exhaustion, Gibbs/testing transfers, and one final occupied-leverage localization attempt. Finite evaluated-row second moments and a one-dimensional higher-moment divergence result were derived, but the shrinking weighted complement, ordinary-posterior contraction, and all-data multiplier rates remain open; calibration was neither proved nor refuted. Independent validity review terminated this positive run as proof-incomplete, solver_blocked/retry, with no achieved novelty tier and no Lean formalization.
tldr: For the causal incremental-odds curve, the unchanged SoftBart 1.0.3 ideal posterior is proper and has finite evaluated counterfactual second moments under the declared positive-density class. A new exact boundary-pocket lemma proves infinite third and higher moments at an opposite-arm row and infinite unlocalized regression fourth-norm integrals in one dimension. Explicit weighted exhaustion, observed-loss localization, and a local rank-grid score rate are proved. The final leverage attempt gives an all-topology weighted tail only at an exponentially large cutoff, so the contracting ordinary-posterior kernel remains open even in the sufficient regime \(d<2\min(\alpha,1)\). Posterior mean, SD, covariance, and whole-curve band calibration remain pending consequences in that regime; dimensions \(d\ge2\) remain unresolved.
gap: High-posterior-mass bounded score sieves do not establish sample-size-weighted second moments on their complement. Ordinary-posterior contraction for the exact fixed forests, empirical ranks, and Gaussian working likelihood is not established by the available donors.
fill: The kernel integrates occupied and redundant leaf directions before bounding scales and topology mass. It then derives the discarded-draw and all-data score bounds, making efficient-process transfer a consequence rather than an assumed regularity condition.
